chunk_findings.detail: The degraded-mark assertion was changed from checking the full mark contents to checking only `reviewer`, `reason`, and `at`. A faulty `_note_degraded` implementation that adds the new `at` timestamp but accidentally stops recording the previously asserted `gate`, `model`, and `family` fields would still pass this regression test. The task is only to add expiry/re-probe, so those pre-existing evidence-contract fields should still be asserted rather than deleted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_quota_failover.py:103

chunk_findings.detail: The last assertion requires a pre-fix degraded mark with no `at` timestamp to remain in `active_degraded_marks` at `now=9_999_999.0` with a 3600s cooldown. That is the original B066719c493 permanence bug for already-persisted degraded reviewers: a missing timestamp can never age past any cooldown, so existing grok-4.7/gemini/kimi marks are shed forever. The test as written blesses the broken behavior instead of verifying that an old no-timestamp mark is stamped or expires after a cooldown, so a correct fix would fail this assertion or the implementation would leave the original bug in place for existing marks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_quota_failover.py:test_a_degraded_mark_expires_after_the_cooldown

chunk_findings.detail: The change is the fix for bug B066719c493, which is explicitly a bug-fix task, but the six-file manifest contains no task file with a phase, stated `needs`/`no-deps`, and `wave:N` tag. Rule r-task-phase-needs-wave requires every bug-fix task to carry that metadata, so the task is not phase-taggable and the change is incomplete for the task workflow.
chunk_findings.title: <change manifest> [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: A degraded row written before this change has no `at`, and the predicate `row.get("at") is None` keeps it active forever, regardless of `degraded_cooldown_s`. This preserves the exact permanent-shed bug for already-degraded reviewers: an environment that already recorded a transient 429 for grok-4.7 will continue to re-shed it on every review after upgrading, because the old timestamp-less mark never expires and the reviewer is never re-probed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:active_degraded_marks

chunk_findings.detail: `degraded_notes` still iterates `degraded_marks(state)` rather than only active marks, so an expired mark still produces “reviewer X is degraded … shed from its gates.” For example, with `cooldown_s=3600`, a mark at epoch `T` and `now = T + 7200` is not returned by `active_degraded_marks`, but `degraded_notes` still reports it as currently degraded and shed, contradicting the new expiry behavior and misleading operator/doctor output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:degraded_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The new `[review]` table header is emitted before the existing root-level `[[reviewer]]` entries. In TOML, after `[review]`, each `[[reviewer]]` is parsed as `review.reviewer`, not as the root `reviewer` array DDflow reads. So `_setup(repo, tmp_path)` now writes a config with no root reviewers; the review run under test will fail/misbehave before the degraded-cooldown logic is exercised. Move the `[review]` section after the reviewer tables, or define reviewers explicitly under the namespace the schema actually expects.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_quota_failover.py:_config

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion that a degraded mark with no `at` timestamp remains active at `now=9_999_999.0` codifies the exact bug B066719c493 is supposed to fix. Pre-fix degraded evidence has no timestamp, so an already-degraded reviewer would be treated as permanently fresh, never expire, and never be re-probed. The test should expect a missing timestamp to be re-probed after the cooldown (or to receive a new timestamp), not to remain degraded forever.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_quota_failover.py::test_a_degraded_mark_expires_after_the_cooldown

It treats `rubber_duck`'s last `review_degraded` row as the first-run baseline and `critic`'s last row as the re-probe, then only requires `second[-1]["at"] > first[-1]["at"]`. A run that never re-probes (or re-invokes the CLI and then drops the second degradation note) therefore still has that first-run critic row. If `rubber_duck` was marked earlier in that same first pass, critic's `at` is already strictly newer, so all three asserts pass with `len(second) == 1` and no second `review_degraded` row. Compare a snapshot of critic's own mark from before the second review, or require `len(second) > len(before)` and `second[-1]["at"] > before[-1]["at"]`.

chunk_findings.detail: The re-mark check still does not require a fresh timestamp. After the critic review it only requires `len(critic_after) == len(critic_before) + 1` and `critic_after[-1]["reviewer"] == "exhausted"`. The comment says a dropped re-mark leaves the revision mark's `at` unchanged, and the bug requires that re-probe to write a fresh degradation so the reviewer stays shed until the next cooldown. A run that re-invokes the CLI (`----` count increases) and appends `{"reviewer": "exhausted", "at": <the same expired timestamp already on critic_before[-1]>}` satisfies both asserts, so the next gate still treats the mark as expired. Nothing compares `critic_after[-1]["at"]` to `critic_before[-1]["at"]` or to the cooldown boundary.
